mode: full audit and candidate readiness; no remediation or publication
standards: OWASP Top 10:2021 crosswalk, retained for prior-audit comparability

findings.title: Hardlink aliases bypass ownership and workspace write confinement
findings.description: The direct write tool authorizes a resolved pathname, then truncates the existing inode. A hardlink inside an allowed lane can name an operator-owned inode or an inode outside the workspace. Path.resolve() does not distinguish hardlinks; the in-process write is outside the OS sandbox.
findings.preconditions: An admitted workspace contains a preexisting hardlink to a protected same-filesystem file. No control of environment variables or a real service is required.
findings.evidence: containment.py: both operator_lane_changed and outside_workspace_changed are true after successful write_file dispatch.
findings.mitigation: Use same-directory exclusive temporary files and atomic replacement so writes replace only the authorized directory entry; reject or explicitly handle multiply linked files and anchor directory traversal. Preserve permissions deliberately. Review shell-created hardlinks separately under native backends.
findings.regression: Hardlink to operator lane, another agent claim and outside-workspace file; symlink/parent replacement variants; ordinary edits and deliberate legitimate hardlinks as compatibility controls.

findings.title: Cross-origin redirects retain provider credentials
findings.description: All production adapters use the default urllib redirect handler. A 302 can move a credentialed POST to another origin while retaining Authorization or X-api-key headers.
findings.preconditions: The configured provider, proxy or endpoint redirects. This is conditional credential disclosure, not an arbitrary attacker-selected URL in a prompt.
findings.evidence: transport.py uses the actual HTTPRedirectHandler.redirect_request with synthetic headers: changes_origin, retains_authorization and retains_x_api_key are all true. No request was sent.
findings.mitigation: Reject redirects by default, reusing the pilot no-redirect design. Any supported redirect must use an explicit same-origin HTTPS policy and remove sensitive headers before crossing trust boundaries.
findings.regression: 301/302/303/307/308, cross-origin and HTTPS downgrade, same-origin policy, custom credential headers, safe local positive controls.

findings.title: Admitted evidence is not bound to the bytes later read
findings.description: Preflight verifies proof digests but stores paths. The evidence tool reopens those paths without a digest, no-follow or containment recheck. Checks execute after preflight, and evidence_root may be inside the mutable workspace. The final bundle digest is also reread from its path.
findings.preconditions: A check or another writer can modify an admitted proof or parent after admission. The direct repro swaps a proof for a symlink to a disposable outside-root file. A check can rewrite admitted evidence without a concurrent race.
findings.evidence: governance.py evidence_post_admission_swap returns ok=true and returned_outside_bytes=true.
findings.mitigation: Snapshot bounded immutable evidence and bundle bytes at admission, and serve/hash that snapshot. If reopening is unavoidable, use anchored no-follow descriptors and verify the exact consumed bytes and containment.
findings.regression: Post-admission content/file/parent replacement, check-modified proof, bundle replacement, outside-root symlink, unchanged-proof positive control.

findings.title: Parallel Responses conversations share mutable replay state
findings.description: The runner caches one model object per spec while parallel loops share it. A delayed A response can overwrite B replay state after B has completed, while the object still identifies B as its current conversation. B follow-up then transmits A prompt/output and drops its own original context and instructions.
findings.preconditions: Two concurrent phases use the same openai-responses tier. No malformed provider response is needed.
findings.evidence: responses-race.py uses deterministic thread barriers and a fake opener: b_followup_contains_a_private_input=true, b_followup_omits_b_original_input=true, instructions_still_b=false.
findings.mitigation: Give each loop/conversation its own adapter and replay state. A lock around an individual complete() call alone does not preserve histories across interleaved conversations.
findings.regression: Barrier-driven same-tier concurrent loops, delayed responses, repeated tool turns, failures and sequential conversation reuse. Assert no cross-conversation input, output or instructions.

findings.title: Workflow preapproval overrides explicit or invalid approval policy
findings.description: The handler grants approve_tools before consulting the explicit approval policy. This contradicts the policy contract that explicit deny wins and bypasses malformed-policy denial as well.
findings.preconditions: An operator-supplied workflow includes a preapproval and a separately supplied policy denies that tool. This is a composition/precedence defect, not a claim that workflows are untrusted by default.
findings.evidence: governance.py supplies a deny for expire_fact plus workflow preapproval; the fact is actually archived.
findings.mitigation: Evaluate invalid-policy and explicit-deny results first. Consider workflow grants, policy allows and TTY only after mandatory denial checks.
findings.regression: Global/phase deny crossed with workflow grant, policy allow and TTY; malformed policy plus grant; valid allow positive control.

findings.title: Resume reuses accepted results after task or goal changes
findings.description: Ordinary resume skips any passed phase with the same name. It does not bind the prior acceptance to workflow/goal/rendered task/criteria or current artifact bytes.
findings.preconditions: The same run ID is resumed after contract or artifact drift. This can happen accidentally; it does not require rewriting the hash chain.
findings.evidence: governance.py changes the task and goal, then resumes with an empty mock brain: skipped_resume, zero model calls, old report reused.
findings.mitigation: Persist a versioned run contract and relevant input/artifact digests, validate them before reusing completed phases, and refuse incompatible resumes with a new-run remedy. Do not silently rerun side effects.
findings.regression: Changed goal/task/check/criteria/upstream report/artifact, reordered phases, unchanged resume positive control.

findings.title: Raw tool secrets and PII enter the event log before containment
findings.description: tool_result logs the first 300 characters before the containment call. read_file returns raw content. A subsequent secret_egress halt prevents the next model call but does not remove the credential already in events.jsonl. Recognized PII is also logged before stripping.
findings.preconditions: An agent reads an in-workspace file containing a recognized credential or PII near the beginning. Local logs then carry sensitive material and may later be shared.
findings.evidence: containment.py: raw_value_in_events=true for both credential and email; credential stops at secret_egress after one mock call, PII completes after two.
findings.mitigation: Contain/redact before every event emission and model boundary; log only safe kind labels and metadata on refusal. Audit other exception/refusal/event paths for the same ordering.
findings.regression: Read-file, evidence-reader, plugin and shell results with canaries at multiple offsets; inspect every artifact and captured model request, not only final stop status.

findings.title: PII stripping can hide a recognized secret and retain it for rehydration
findings.description: guard_egress strips PII before scanning secrets. A credential whose suffix matches the credit-card detector can lose its recognizable shape, enter the strip map and later be reconstructed.
findings.preconditions: A recognized credential overlaps a PII pattern. The repro uses a synthetic Anthropic-shaped prefix and a Luhn-valid numeric suffix.
findings.evidence: containment.py: recognized_before_strip=true, guard_returned_without_halt=true, mapping_entries=1, rehydration_reconstructs_secret=true.
findings.mitigation: Detect/refuse secret spans on the original text before PII replacement and validate mappings never contain secret material. Preserve PII-only behavior.
findings.regression: Every credential kind crossed with overlapping email/phone/card patterns and offsets, plus ordinary PII and nonsecret numeric positive controls.

findings.title: Resume resets cumulative spend and token accounting
findings.description: Each runner constructs a fresh Budget without replaying historical usage. A resumed run therefore starts with full configured headroom despite prior usage.
findings.preconditions: A run with prior spend is resumed. This differs from the documented per-call overshoot residual: the entire earlier accumulated spend is lost.
findings.evidence: governance.py logs 100000 tokens and $5 for the prior run; the resumed counters are zero.
findings.mitigation: Reconstruct cumulative usage from validated history before dispatch, refuse unknown/malformed accounting, and bind budget changes to explicit recorded operator action.
findings.regression: Exhausted resume makes zero calls; exact partial headroom; repeated resumes; parallel usage counted once; missing usage handling.

findings.title: Provider failure or refusal envelopes become executable tool turns
findings.description: Tool presence overrides content_filter/refusal or is checked ahead of failed/cancelled/incomplete status. The normalized turn can reach tool dispatch or task_complete despite a blocked provider status.
findings.preconditions: A provider or compatibility server returns a contradictory tool-bearing error/refusal envelope. The adapters are responsible for rejecting malformed states.
findings.evidence: transport.py: all three blocked envelopes become tool_use and retain task_complete.
findings.mitigation: Give terminal refusal/failure precedence and reject contradictory envelopes while preserving available accounting separately. Validate response and individual tool item status.
findings.regression: Provider status x tool-presence x usage matrix, truncated and contradictory envelopes, valid tool-use positive controls; assert zero dispatch on refused/error turns.

findings.title: Absent provider usage is silently counted as zero
findings.description: All production adapters accept absent usage as empty data and default absent counters to zero. Metered runs continue with unverifiable accounting.
findings.preconditions: A provider omits usage or one counter. Some local compatibility services legitimately lack accounting, which needs an explicit unmetered mode rather than an implicit zero.
findings.evidence: transport.py: missing_usage_accepted and missing_usage_counted_as_zero are true for all three adapters.
findings.mitigation: Represent unknown accounting explicitly; fail closed for metered runs or require an explicit unmetered policy. Preserve received counters even if unrelated parsing fails.
findings.regression: Missing/null/partial/negative/bool/string/nonfinite counters, known-zero positive control, malformed result with intact usage, no retry after accounting uncertainty.

findings.title: Transport, file and child-output limits truncate only after unbounded reads
findings.description: Production HTTP success/error reads are unbounded, read_file/read_evidence read full files before slicing, and subprocess capture_output accumulates all output before truncation. Socket timeout is not a whole-call deadline. Large or slow data can exhaust memory or monopolize a run.
findings.preconditions: A provider, check or admitted file generates excessive or slow-trickling data. No live stress test was performed.
findings.evidence: transport.py records resp.read() invoked with no size. Remaining call sites were directly inspected; no exhaustion payload was run.
findings.mitigation: Stream with byte ceilings and overflow sentinel, use whole-call supervision, bound both stdout and stderr, and supervise/clean the process group. Reuse tested pilot concepts without copying unchecked assumptions.
findings.regression: Exact-limit/one-over success and error bodies/files, false Content-Length, slow trickle, large stdout/stderr and exited-parent live-pipe fixtures; check cleanup and bounded memory.

findings.title: Adversarial convergence ignores explicit stand-down
findings.description: The parser coerces no_new_objection with bool(), while the runner ignores it. Empty objection lists count as quiet even when the participant explicitly says false or omits the marker.
findings.preconditions: Recommending positions are followed by empty objections with false/missing stand-down.
findings.evidence: governance.py: such a decision returns passed.
findings.mitigation: Require literal boolean true and an empty validated objection list from every participant for quiet convergence. Missing/false/malformed responses continue only within bounds or require arbitration.
findings.regression: False/missing/string/null stand-down, nonempty objections plus true, malformed objection items and unanimous literal-true positive control.

findings.title: Model summary fabricates decision metadata and independence claim
findings.description: Model-controlled summary text is interpolated as unfenced Markdown metadata. Newlines/headings can introduce invented positions/providers. The linter then derives independence from the rendered structure.
findings.preconditions: An adversarial participant places record syntax in its summary, rather than only in fenced prose.
findings.evidence: governance.py: one actual position yields no lint errors and an independent-positions claim after an injected heading/provider.
findings.mitigation: Render summaries as escaped single-line scalars; derive trusted claims from structured PositionRecord objects, and separately lint imported text. Validate all interpolated fields.
findings.regression: LF/CRLF headings, metadata lists, frontmatter and fence syntax; actual metadata cardinality equals structured input; invented providers cannot earn claims.

findings.title: Final verifier boundary contradicts claim-level verdict instructions
findings.description: The structured default verifier prompt is followed by a generic boundary demanding legacy passed/reasons JSON. Evidence bundles reject that legacy shape.
findings.preconditions: Model-backed evidence-bundle verification. This is a directly confirmed prompt composition conflict, not a measured live model failure rate.
findings.evidence: governance.py: the composed prompt contains claims instructions but ends by requiring legacy boolean JSON.
findings.mitigation: Separate behavior constraints from mode-specific serialization and compose a single explicit output contract.
findings.regression: Inspect the actual composed prompts for each mode; strict claim verdict and legacy-criteria fixtures; no live model call needed.

findings.title: Unavailable check executable is classified as failed artifact
findings.description: Missing executable is converted into a failed check and exit 1, although the standalone contract assigns blocked/infrastructure cases to cannot-verify exit 2.
findings.preconditions: A configured check program is not installed. The safe repro bypasses only the sandbox wrapper for a nonexistent executable; nothing executes.
findings.evidence: governance.py: missing check returns exit_code=1, expected_cannot_verify=2.
findings.mitigation: Introduce structured check outcomes for completed failure, blocked infrastructure, timeout and resource stop; avoid classifying via message prefixes.
findings.regression: Nonexistent binary, malformed command, permission error, timeout, sandbox refusal, genuine executable exit-1 positive control.

findings.title: Search checker decodes XML entities more than once
findings.description: The chained decoder handles amp before lt/gt. Nested escapes therefore change meaning, and apostrophe/numeric references are incomplete.
findings.preconditions: A local sitemap or metadata contains nested or numeric XML references. This is a retained handoff defect, not a demonstrated runtime security compromise.
findings.evidence: assurance.py evaluates the current function: nested XML escape decodes twice.
findings.mitigation: Patch only the decoder using upstream asset v7 single-pass XML/numeric decoding, retain local adaptations, and route production canonical parsing through the same contract when changed.
findings.regression: Nested amp escape, apos, decimal/hex numeric references, invalid Unicode, whitespace around loc and encoded live canonical.

findings.title: Eval runners silently ignore unknown assertion fields
findings.description: Most scenario kinds run only a fixed subset of expectations without rejecting unsupported expect_* keys. A misspelled or unsupported security assertion can produce green despite never being tested. Observer/AIDR cases already reject unknown assertions.
findings.preconditions: An eval author adds or misspells an expected security condition.
findings.evidence: assurance.py: a loop scenario with expect_impossible_security_property passes unchanged.
findings.mitigation: Validate a versioned per-kind scenario schema, reject unknown fields/duplicate IDs, require nonvacuous assertions, and add mutation checks proving every expectation can fail.
findings.regression: Unknown/misspelled assertion for every kind, wrong types, duplicate scenario IDs, inverted assertions on every shipped fixture.

findings.title: Audit claims overstate detection without a trusted tail anchor
findings.description: A prev-linked chain cannot detect edits to its terminal event or suffix truncation without a separately trusted tail/count. Documentation says any edit/deletion is detected while disclosing only whole-file rewrite as a limit.
findings.preconditions: An actor can modify the event file. This is an inherent unanchored-chain residual and a claim/test gap, not a new privilege bypass.
findings.evidence: governance.py: edited_tail_accepted=true and truncated_tail_accepted=true.
findings.mitigation: Narrow claims to linked interior changes. Optionally verify an externally trusted terminal digest/count or signed completion receipt; do not store the only anchor beside the mutable log.
findings.regression: Interior edit, last-event edit, suffix truncation, empty log and trusted-tail mismatch; retain valid-resume positive control.

findings.title: Nonfinite numeric configuration passes validation
findings.description: YAML NaN/infinity passes numeric schema comparisons and simple <=0 checks. Nonfinite dollar ceilings/rates invalidate dollar accounting comparisons.
findings.preconditions: Operator-authored config includes .nan/.inf. Token limits still apply; no unlimited-spend remote exploit is claimed.
findings.evidence: assurance.py: NaN budget validates and does not exhaust even with large spend.
findings.mitigation: Reject nonfinite numeric values recursively before schema use; enforce finite nonnegative accounting updates and explicit ceiling semantics.
findings.regression: NaN/+inf/-inf, negative/bool/string counters and rates, finite zero/positive controls.

findings.title: Release tooling lock contains a setuptools advisory
findings.description: pip-audit flags setuptools 84.0.0 for GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w; fixed in 84.1.0. Advisory describes Windows legacy wheel-install metadata path traversal creating fixed-content __init__.py outside the destination.
findings.preconditions: The vulnerable legacy installation path runs on Windows with a crafted wheel. Harnessie supports macOS/Linux shell workflows; this is a low-applicability build-tool maintenance finding, not runtime compromise on this host.
findings.evidence: Fresh pip-audit JSON retained. No exploit was run and no real credential accessed.
findings.mitigation: Refresh both hash-locked tooling profiles to 84.1.0 through the repo lock generator, review the lock delta and run installed-lock, build and fresh-install gates.
findings.regression: Lock manifest consistency, supported-platform resolution, zero-advisory rescan and package smoke.

additional_eval_opportunities.evidence: assurance.py; present counters are files/bytes, so treat as contract precision and resource-bound extension rather than claiming existing file counter arithmetic is wrong.

additional_eval_opportunities.evidence: Static _snapshot reads whole regular files; artifact-volume limits are post-operation net snapshots, not peak disk/memory limits.
